summary: Add one molecular curly-arrow figure, misconception-based reaction terminology practice, and a targeted electrophilic-addition arrow check.

improvements.caption: Hydroxide lone pair attacks a proton: follow the curly arrow from oxygen to hydrogen
improvements.where: note, after the nucleophile and electrophile definitions in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: The inspected crop is legible and self-contained; it shows a molecular electron-pair source and destination that the available diagram types cannot draw. The note should tell learners to notice that the arrow tail is at the oxygen lone pair.
All seven existing KC 13.2.1 items are short answers; there is no misconception-distractor recognition practice for bond fission or reaction types.
improvements.what: Add generated MCQs with mapped misconception distractors: one distinguishes homolysis and heterolysis from electron allocation and products; one classifies addition, substitution, elimination or hydrolysis from a short reaction description. Give specific explanations and three progressive hints.

improvements.why: The existing method states the general curly-arrow rule but does not walk through the commonly reversed first arrow in alkene electrophilic addition.
improvements.what: Append a compact HCl-to-alkene arrow check: the first full curly arrow starts at the C=C pi bond and points to H of H-Cl; the H-Cl bond electron pair moves to Cl. Do not start the first arrow at HCl or at a bonded atom. Keep it a generic mechanism convention, leaving product selectivity to the later alkene chapter.
improvements.source: ER 9701 s22 P23 Q4 in bundle; Cambridge International 9701 2025-2027 syllabus section 13.2: https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/664563-2025-2027-syllabus.pdf
